morph_sequence — SHAPE2D morph op

• Data kinds: image2d × image2d × pairs × pairs → images

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.morph_sequence(imgA, imgB, ptsA, ptsB, n=7, method='affine', lam=0.0, with_corners=True) (to call the implementation directly, import imagemorph; imagemorph.morph_sequence(imgA, imgB, ptsA, ptsB, n=7, method='affine', lam=0.0, with_corners=True); from the registry, opsshape2d.get("morph_sequence"))

Usage

Morph sequence with alpha swept 0→1 in n steps (frames that change smoothly from A to B).

Returns: a list of length n. The first matches A, the last matches B.

It simply calls morph(imgA, imgB, ptsA, ptsB, alpha, method, lam, with_corners) for each value of alpha = linspace(0, 1, n). Each frame has 3 stages: (1) build the intermediate points (1-α) ptsA + α ptsB, (2) warp A and B each onto them,

(3) cross-dissolve with α. Each frame does 2 warps, so

the cost is proportional to n (14 warps for n=7).

• imgA, imgB: (H, W[, C]), same shape, [0, 1]. NaN/Inf are silently replaced by 0 / 1.

• ptsA, ptsB: (K, 2) (x, y), corresponding points of same count and order.

• n: 2 or more (1 or less gives ValueError). Truncated to int.

• method: "affine" (Delaunay piecewise affine, fast) / "tps" (thin-plate spline, smooth). Anything else gives ValueError. lam is the TPS smoothing coefficient (0 for exact interpolation).

• with_corners: True adds add_frame_corners to both point sets, preventing holes outside the frame.

• Returns: a list of n float64 arrays (type images). Already clipped to [0, 1].

If you want just 1 image (e.g. the intermediate face at α = 0.5), use morph directly.
